scores.round_files_fidelity_rationale: Up 0.2. Gained: clipper.rs is the most faithful large port so far. I walked every method against clipper.cs. The arena translation keeps reference identity everywhere it matters: OutRec index == m_PolyOuts index because both are pushed and cleared together, GetOutRec compares indices the way C# compares references, and JoinPoints writes through m_Joins[j] so the OutPt1/OutPt2 updates persist as they do on the C# Join object. JoinCommonEdges re-reads the join after JoinPoints. AppendPolygon, DoSimplePolygons and FixupFirstLefts1/2/3 read live fields wherever C# does. Int128Mul, the explicit double operator and neg match bit for bit with wrapping u64 arithmetic, including C#'s overflow in c. Round() and IntPoint(double,double) use cast_i64 (cvttsd2si semantics). TopX, IntersectPoint, GetDx, Area(OutPt) ((double)(long+long)), PointInPolygon ((double)(long-long)) and DistanceFromLineSqrd convert to double at the same points as C#. IsMaxima/IsIntermediate compare Top.Y as a double, as C#'s double parameter does. ProcessIntersections returns without clearing m_SortedEdges on the early returns, as C#'s return inside try does. ClipperOffset's outer-rectangle removal keeps m_AllPolys, so Total still drops the hidden outer node. EnumTranslator.GetDisplayText now finds the field by name. Lost: (a) the port is unwired, and FlightPlanner's offset polygon (menu.rs:94-131) is still an equirectangular miter approximation with no clipping (R69-02). (b) PolyTreeToPaths copies contours, so Grid.cs:264's in-place ReversePaths(PolyTreeToPaths(tree)) cannot be reproduced (R69-03). (c) The List.Sort port passes count instead of the List's capacity (R69-04). (d) A stale m_Scanbeam index after a failed Execute can panic on reuse. Panics replace exceptions in several places, and the exception types differ (R69-05). (e) The public API has gaps (R69-06). (f) GetDisplayText still takes an i64, there is no alias test, and culture_compare is still an approximation (R69-07).
scores.ui_ux_rationale: Up 0.1. CMB_altmode can no longer show blank: an out-of-list alt_frame is normalised to list[0] (Relative), and processToScreen falls back to Relative for a frame outside EnumToList, as CMB_altmode_SelectedIndexChanged does in C#. Still wrong: 'Offset Polygon' in the FlightPlanner map menu produces different geometry from C#. C# offsets in UTM metres scaled by 1000, truncates the offset to Int64 millimetres, clips self-intersections through the ClipperOffset union, returns without change when the tree is empty, and concatenates every child contour. Rust offsets in a local equirectangular frame and never clips, so a negative offset past a narrow neck shows crossed edges instead of disappearing or splitting. The title, markers, rally warning and GCSView items from round 68 are unchanged.

compile_check.summary: I checked clipper.rs (4,797 lines) as the compiler, plus the round-68 changes. Types and derives: TEdge, IntersectNode, LocalMinima, Scanbeam, Maxima, OutRec, OutPt and Join all derive Copy, so the many 'let x = self.arena[i];' copies type-check. IntersectNode derives Default + Clone (usize, IntPoint: Default), which satisfies introspective_sort's T: Default + Clone. PolyNode derives Default, and that holds because JoinType and EndType derive Default with #[default] variants and m_Parent is Option<usize>. EdgeSide/Direction derive PartialEq for ==. Int128 derives PartialEq, and its unused operators sit under #[allow(dead_code)]. Paths: crate::dotnet::{cast_i64, math_max, math_min, index_out_of_range, Exception::Custom/IndexOutOfRange} exist (mod.rs:715/727/764/1517/850). collections::introspective_sort(&mut [T], usize, F) (collections.rs:126) accepts &mut self.m_IntersectList through deref coercion to &mut [IntersectNode]. The closure's Ok(..) error type comes from the F bound. Borrow checking: the immediately invoked closures in AddPath (926, captures only ufr/pg/highI, not self), Execute_paths (1466), Execute_tree_fill (1490), ExecuteInternal (1520) and ProcessIntersections (2847) capture self (and solution/polytree) uniquely. Each is a temporary dropped at the end of its let, before the following self.DisposeAllPolyPts()/self.m_Joins.clear()/self.m_SortedEdges = NIL. JoinHorz's nx = |s: &Self, o| and JoinPoints's o = |s: &Self, p| capture nothing, and calls with the &mut self receiver coerce &mut Clipper to &Clipper at the closure call (the signature is annotated). They hold no borrow across self.DupOutPt(..). IsContributing's zero_side/inside closures borrow e: &TEdge alongside shared reads of self. PointInPolygon's d closures borrow ip/ipNext (poly0x/poly1x) and are dead before those are reassigned. CleanPolygon's exclude takes pts as a parameter and captures nothing. Statements like self.edges[e].Curr.X = Self::TopX(&self.edges[e], topY) evaluate the right-hand side first, so the shared borrow ends before IndexMut. self.m_destPolys.push(std::mem::take(&mut self.m_destPoly)) borrows disjoint fields. In DoOffset's zero-delta loop, node = &self.m_polyNodes.nodes[*c] is disjoint from self.m_destPolys. Deferred init: 'let (lb, rb);' (1062), 'let result; let e; let prevE;' (2045) and 'let mut EStart;' (810) are each assigned on every path before use. Name resolution: parameters named Direction (2798), Dir, Pt and X/Y are value-namespace bindings, and Direction::dLeftToRight still resolves the enum through the type namespace. lowercase consts (horizontal, Skip) are allowed by #![allow(non_upper_case_globals)]. Visibility: ClipperOffset and Clipper touch PolyTree's private nodes/m_AllPolys/m_Childs and call the private new_node/AddChild from the same module, which is allowed. The tests use only pub API (ChildCount, Childs, Contour, IsHole, Area, PointInPolygon, CleanPolygon, Orientation, Execute*, AddPath). Test expectations, checked by hand: the square tests give intersection 2500, union 17500, difference 7500 and xor 15000 (the sum of two L-shapes). The -100 jtMiter offset puts winding +1 inside x,y in [100,900] against the -1 outer rectangle, so pftNegative leaves an 800x800 hole that the outer-node removal promotes, and it is not a hole after promotion. At -600 the self-intersecting offset ring has winding <= 0 everywhere (for example -3 at (500,500), 0 just outside the square), so only the outer rectangle remains and Clear() empties the tree. At +100, the miter limit is 0.5 and r = 1, so DoMiter puts the corners at (-100,-100)..(1100,1100), giving 1200x1200. PointInPolygon gives (5,5) = 1, (0,5) = -1 (d == 0 on the x=0 edge) and (15,5) = 0. CleanPolygon removes (5,0) (DistanceFromLineSqrd 0 < 2.002), and the other vertices give 20 and 50, so 4 points remain. The open-path Execute errs, and AddPath(open, ptClip) errs. Round-68 changes: EnumFieldInfo gained name: String. Both constructors (mission.rs:78-83 and the test, 157-159) supply it, and Debug/Clone still derive. GetDisplayText's fields.iter().find(|f| f.name == name) compares String == String. The flight_plan.rs fallback reads altmode_list() -> Vec<(i32, String)>, and list.first().map(|(k, _)| *k as u8) is an Option<u8>. In the CMB_altmode closure, the normalisation assigns app.settings.alt_frame before cur is read, through the same capture the existing click handler already uses. No definite compile error.

findings.summary: New. ClipperOffset is ported but unwired. FlightPlanner's offset-polygon handler still calls the hand-rolled offset_polygon (menu.rs:94-131). That function projects equirectangularly around the first vertex, not through PointLatLngAlt.ToUTM/utmpos with a closing point. It works in f64 metres instead of IntPoint(x*1000, y*1000) with the offset truncated to (Int64)(intmeter*1000). It never clips: there is no union with pftPositive/pftNegative and no outer rectangle, so a negative offset past a neck keeps crossing edges instead of vanishing or splitting. It does not return when tree.ChildCount == 0, does not concatenate every child contour, and does not tag the points 'S' for redrawPolygonSurvey. Its orientation fix-up (reverse when the shoelace area < 0) is not FixOrientations, and its miter fallback squares corners with two points instead of DoSquare's tan(atan2(..)/4) construction.
findings.required_fix: Replace offset_polygon with the C# flow: UTM zone of list[0], utmpos list closed with list[0], ClipperOffset::new(2.0, 0.25).AddPath(IntPoint::from_f64(x*1000, y*1000), jtMiter, etClosedPolygon), Execute_tree(&mut tree, cast_i64(intmeter*1000) as f64). Return if ChildCount(ROOT) == 0, otherwise concatenate every child's Contour/1000 back to LLA with Tag 'S'. Add a test that a -600 m offset of a 1 km square leaves the polygon unchanged.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Utilities/clipper.cs:4400-4444 (paths.Add(polynode.m_polygon) shares the node's List), 3336-3340 (ReversePaths reverses in place); ExtLibs/Utilities/Grid.cs:264
findings.summary: New. PolyTreeToPaths, ClosedPathsFromPolyTree and OpenPathsFromPolyTree clone each contour. C# adds the node's own m_polygon List, so a Paths built from the tree aliases the tree. Grid.cs:264 depends on that: ClipperLib.Clipper.ReversePaths(ClipperLib.Clipper.PolyTreeToPaths(tree)) reverses tree.Childs[i].Contour in place, and the following loop reads those contours to build clockwise laps. With this API, the same call reverses a temporary copy, so a Grid port would silently lose the lap direction. Separately, PolyTree::Contour returns &Path, so C# code that mutates Contour cannot be expressed at all.
findings.required_fix: Give the tree an aliasing-equivalent operation, for example PolyTree::ReverseAllContours(nt) or a Contour_mut, and have the Grid port use it. Document the deviation in PolyTreeToPaths. Add a test that ReversePaths(PolyTreeToPaths(tree)) as Grid uses it leaves tree.Contour reversed.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Utilities/clipper.cs:3050 (m_IntersectList.Sort(m_IntersectNodeComparer)), 1389, 3083 (List.Clear keeps capacity); .NET 4.x ArraySortHelper.IntrospectiveSort depth = 2 * FloorLog2(keys.Length)
findings.summary: New. FixupIntersectionOrder passes backing_len = m_IntersectList.len(). List<T>.Sort sorts _items, whose Length is the List's capacity. m_IntersectList is created once per Clipper and cleared, not reallocated, after each scanbeam (ProcessIntersectList), so its capacity is the high-water mark of 4/8/16/... growth. The depth limit, and so the point where intro_sort switches to heapsort, differs. Since the sort is unstable, intersect nodes with equal Pt.Y can end up in a different order. That changes the order FixupIntersectionOrder swaps edges and ProcessIntersectList calls IntersectEdges. dotnet/collections.rs:118-125 documents this parameter, and clipper.rs ignores it.
findings.required_fix: Track the C# List capacity of m_IntersectList (grow with list_capacity_for_count on push, never shrink on clear) and pass that as backing_len.

findings.cs_reference: ExtLibs/Utilities/clipper.cs:1137-1163 (Reset), 1586-1590 (DisposeAllPolyPts only clears m_PolyOuts), 2958-2978 (catch-all -> ClipperException), 1804/1930/2523/2593/4201 (Math.Abs throws OverflowException), 4378 (pattern[0] -> ArgumentOutOfRangeException)
findings.summary: New. (1) DisposeAllPolyPts also empties the sbs/maxs/outrecs/outpts arenas, but m_Scanbeam/m_ActiveEdges are reset only inside ResetBase when a minima list exists. After an Execute that returns false (FixupIntersectionOrder) or Errs, then Clear(), the next Execute indexes the emptied sbs and panics, where C# continues on the old Scanbeam objects. (2) ProcessIntersections' C# catch converts any exception (NullReference, ArgumentOutOfRange) into ClipperException('ProcessIntersections error'). Rust index panics escape it. (3) Math.Abs(int.MinValue/long.MinValue) throws OverflowException in IsContributing, SetWindingCount, IntersectEdges and SlopesNearCollinear. Rust uses wrapping_abs. (4) MinkowskiSum(pattern, paths, true) with an empty pattern throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException from the List indexer in C#, but Rust returns IndexOutOfRange (4186).
findings.required_fix: Keep a stale-safe reset (set m_Scanbeam/m_ActiveEdges to NIL in DisposeAllPolyPts, or keep the arenas the way C# keeps its objects). Map out-of-range accesses inside ProcessIntersections to the ClipperException. Use checked_abs and return Overflow where C# throws. Use the List indexer's ArgumentOutOfRange message for pattern[0].

verdict: No definite compile error. clipper.rs type-checks: every arena record derives Copy, IntersectNode meets introspective_sort's Default + Clone, the immediately invoked closures that capture self are dropped before the 'finally' statements, the |s: &Self, ..| helper closures capture nothing, and the cross-type private access stays inside one module. The only compiler output expected is a dead_code warning for PointIsVertex/PointOnLineSegment/PointOnPolygon. The four Clipper tests check out by hand (2500/17500/7500/15000, 800x800 hole promoted, -600 empty, 1200x1200 miter, PointInPolygon 1/-1/0, CleanPolygon 4 points). The round-68 enumtranslator test failure is fixed. The Clipper port is a faithful statement-level translation: the arena indices preserve C#'s reference identity, joins mutate through m_Joins[j], Int128 and the long-to-double conversions are bit-exact, and ClipperOffset's outer-node removal keeps m_AllPolys. But nothing calls it. FlightPlanner's offset polygon still runs a hand-rolled, unclipped equirectangular approximation, and Grid.cs is unported. The API also cannot reproduce the aliasing Grid.cs relies on (ReversePaths(PolyTreeToPaths(tree))), and the List.Sort port ignores the List capacity. R68-04's altmode fallback is in. R68-02 is mostly fixed. R68-03 and every older gap are unchanged. Ported lines rise to 32,736 / 479,014 (6.8%), and the cap rises to 1.7. Awarded 1.4; round-file fidelity 6.3; UI/UX 2.5; features 3.4.
